name: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński - § 10 - Am 1
title: REPORT on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2023, Section X – European External Action Service
part_text: 10. Recalls that there have been allegations regarding the involvement of 19 out of 13.000 UNRWA employees in Gaza in the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israel on 7 October 2023; notes that in response to these allegations, and after the investigations of the UN Office of Internal Oversight Services (OIOS), nine staff members had their employment formally terminated by the UNRWA; underlines that the Commission has been working with the UNRWA to improve control systems, in line with recommendations from the OIOS, including the screening of staff, a Union audit by Union-appointed independent internal experts and the strengthening of internal investigative and ethical frameworks; welcomes that all disbursements have been released by the Commission following the full implementation of these conditions, which continues to be monitored by the Commission services; recalls that the taxpayer money is not to be misused; recalls the findings of the Georg Eckert Institute's Union-funded report, which revealed a complex picture on the Palestinian textbooks; notes that the Union does not fund the Palestinian Textbooks, and that neither are they the responsibility of UNRWA, which nevertheless reviews all issued textbooks to address any problematic content; encourages the EEAS to support diplomatic efforts for a comprehensive and sustainable peace based on the International law, protection of civilians and the two-state solution;
